subject: Pinnacle Dedicated: recommended GPU mix, memory/perf tradeoffs and fallbacks
messages:

Subject: Dedicated capacity discussion — memory heavy workloads

Hi Soojin / Dev,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — the team liked the latency stability. We ran some internal load tests overnight and wanted to flag two concrete workload profiles: 

1) Real-time QA assistant (short context, high QPS spikes) — mostly 512-token windows, tolerance for lower precision if latency is very low.
2) Document understanding pipeline (long context ingestion) — 64k token chucks, heavy KV cache and ephemeral memory usage, cost sensitive at scale.

We need a recommended configuration for Dedicated (reserved) capacity that balances these: predictability for business-critical QA and capacity for periodic deep-document jobs. Budget target is ~$60k/mo committed.

Can you send a recommended SKUs mix and any fallback/overflow rules if traffic exceeds reserved slots? Also please attach the cost model you mentioned.

Best,
Sophie
Senior ML Platform, Pinnacle Analytics

From: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>

Date: 2028-05-03T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity discussion — memory heavy workloads

Hi Sophie — thanks for the details.

Summary up front: for the mixed profile you described I recommend a hybrid pool: primarily A100 80GB for the long-context document jobs and a smaller fleet of L4 for the low-latency, high-QPS QA traffic, with a thin H100 layer reserved for bursty large-batch throughput and latency-critical experiments. This balances memory headroom, unit cost, and graceful degradation.

Key bullets:
- A100 (80GB) x 6 nodes (primary): handles the 64k token jobs without aggressive tiling/fragmentation; supports higher batch sizes and KV cache anchoring.
- L4 x 10 nodes (secondary): low-cost, high-concurrency for short-context QA; good latency under light quantization (int8/int4).
- H100 x 2 nodes (burst/fallback): used for heavy multi-sequence batches and throughput-sensitive exports; acts as fallthrough when A100 pool is saturated.

Operational notes:
- Autoscaling policy: keep A100 warm to 60% of reserved slots; burst to H100 via scheduled slots or on-demand credits to avoid SLA breaches.
- Caching: use prefix/KV caching on A100 for document sessions; L4 should rely on a small in-memory cache for short prompts.
- Quantization: recommend model-quant profiles for L4 (int8) and A100 (bf16 or int8 where acceptable). H100 runs bf16 for max perf.

I've attached a quick cost sketch and an ops runbook (spreadsheet) with monthly TCO at the requested $60k/mo target — it shows a conservative vs aggressive sizing.

Next steps: Dev and Karthik, can you validate the concurrency math and node counts? Sophie, if you can share expected 95th percentile QPS and concurrent long-context jobs/day, I can tighten the plan.

Thanks,
Soojin
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Attachments: pinnacle_sku_cost_model_v1.xlsx

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity discussion — memory heavy workloads

Looping in some engineering checks. Quick validation on the sizing assumptions I used in the spreadsheet:

Assumptions I modeled:
- Model: open-llm-large-v2 (approx 70B fp16 baseline).
- A100 80GB effective batch throughput: ~4.5x tokens/s vs L4 for long-context once KV warm. For 64k context runs we assume tiling with a 2x memory overhead.
- L4 (4-bit quant) QPS for 512-token ~160 reqs/sec per card at p95 latency target 120ms.
- H100 peak throughput multiplier ~1.8x vs A100 for large batch 1k-token exports.

Resulting capacity mapping for target concurrency:
- A100 x6 covers 4 concurrent 64k jobs/day with headroom for caching; estimated cost portion ~$38k/mo.
- L4 x10 handles baseline QA with room for 200% burst on short windows; estimated ~$12k/mo.
- H100 x2 reserved for peak overflow and heavy ETL exports; estimated reserved portion ~$8k/mo.

Fallback policy notes:
- Prefer routing long-context to A100. If A100 saturation >85% for 2+ minutes, start routing new long-context jobs to H100; preemptible lower-priority jobs on H100 if required.
- For short-context QA, when L4 latency exceeds p95 threshold, spill to A100 pool with quantized model to preserve SLA.

I'll attach a small latency plot from our profiling run (KV cache warm vs cold) — helps to size concurrency.

-Karthik
Senior ML Engineer, Redwood Inference

Sophie — quick commercial note to align runway with the ops plan.

The hybrid mix Karthik laid out maps to the $60k/mo band with the following terms: 12-month commitment, monthly overage priced at on-demand tiers (we can structure credits for burst H100 use), and a quarterly review to right-size pools using usage telemetry.

If Pinnacle needs stronger fallbacks we can add a reserved H100 slot (convert one L4 -> H100) but that nudges committed monthly to ~$68k/mo. We can propose a compromise: start with the A100-heavy baseline and add a small H100 reserve in Q3 if utilization indicates.

Vivek — will you weigh in on discounting for the committed block (legal/finance will need the rate sheet). Sophie, procurement@pinnacle.ai, is this acceptable from your budget perspective? Happy to jump on a 30-min call to finalize the mutual action plan.

Thanks,
